requirement:
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.

A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
rationale:
The five marked tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope`. I found no gap.

- **Every function or method with a body, including test functions, helpers and default trait methods.**
  - `mod[tests]/fn[methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported]` expects `impl[S]/fn[method]`, `mod[tests]/fn[case]` and `mod[tests]/fn[helper]` to be reported as "zero execution".
  - `mod[tests]/fn[default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not]` expects the default body `#trait[T]/fn[body]` to be reported as "zero execution".
  - `mod[tests]/fn[overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent]` checks nested functions and closures. A nested function's or closure's count does not cover the outer function, and the inner function is reported on its own.
- **Declarations without bodies create no obligations.** The default-trait-body test asserts that `fn[declaration]` never appears in the report. It also calls `inventory` on sources that contain only a declaration, a macro invocation, or a derive. Each of those calls gives the expected result.
- **First-party scope, with the project-root `vendor` directory excluded.** `mod[tests]/fn[post_suite_scope_excludes_root_vendor_but_includes_source_vendor]` shows that `src/vendor/first_party.rs` is reported and the check fails. It also asserts that `- vendor/foreign.rs` is absent. The report lines have the form `- {file}: …` (from `fn[check_saved]`), so that negative assertion matches the real output format.
- **Discovery and parse failures cause failure.**
  - In `mod[tests]/fn[methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported]`, a corrupt Git index makes the check fail and report "cannot discover reference sources".
  - In `mod[tests]/fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]`, a malformed `code.rs` makes the check fail with "cannot parse rust source".
- **Functions that cannot be measured are reported as not measured.**
  - In the default-trait-body test, the `#[cfg(any())]` function is reported as `#fn[excluded]: not measured`, which covers exclusion by build configuration. That obligation then falls under `check.exceptions`, which is cited context and not assessed here.
  - In the unmeasured-files test, a file with executable code but no measurement, and a function missing from the function data, both fail as "not measured".

The tests give each case a matching assertion on the outcome, so all of the subject's obligations are checked.

text: :::{req} check.scope
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.
A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage.parsing
Repository validation parses every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs`
file among the sources reference discovery considers under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root
`vendor` directory. It reports a Rust parse failure rather than silently
skipping the file.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
